title: FETCH
prompt:
Create an exceptionally beautiful, unsettling cinematic 16:9 landscape website cover for the original first-person horror game FETCH. Target canvas 2048x1152. No text, title, logo, HUD, crosshair, borders, or watermark. Premium realistic dark fantasy horror game key art, tangible materials, sophisticated contrast, spectacular lighting and atmospheric depth. One coherent scene, not a montage.
Show the game's defining act: a cursed HUMAN SKULL returning through the darkness toward the player's outstretched empty hand, with a small old iron KEY CLAMPED IN ITS TEETH. The skull is the clear foreground focal point, slightly left of centre, large enough to show beautifully detailed aged ivory bone, believable anatomy, subtle old fractures and a complete lower jaw. Its light is a restrained cold blue-white glow from within the eye sockets and mouth that spills physically onto the nearby stone, sleeve and fingers. Avoid neon laser eyes, enormous magical fire, or cartoon skull proportions. A few suspended rain drops and a slight motion streak behind it suggest the last instant of the return; the bone and key remain crisp. The player is seen only through two anatomically correct dirty bare adult hands and frayed grey coat cuffs at the lower edge: one palm open to catch the skull, the other braced on the weathered doorway. No other weapon.
We stand just inside the broken threshold of a decaying house, looking into a moonlit overgrown graveyard and toward a black iron gate. The foreground doorframe and cracked plaster, wet mossy gravestones, delicate ferns and rusted railings have exquisite tactile detail. The skull's departing and returning illumination makes darkness feel like the actual danger. In the right middle distance beyond the gate stands the Resident: a roughly 2.5-metre-tall, gaunt malformed human silhouette in a long dark tattered coat, elongated limbs and a slightly bowed head, patient and disturbing, eyes not glowing. Keep it partially lost in shadow yet recognisably humanoid, not a giant beast. Behind it dense twisted forest seems to close around the path. A few upper windows of the decayed house catch faint moonlight, one far room a weak amber ember, no modern city. Deep navy-black shadows, icy bone light, wet silver moon highlights, a very small trace of warm interior light for balance. Composition should feel like a dangerous journey between house, graves and forest, anchored by this extraordinary skull that is simultaneously a weapon, a lamp and a key carrier. No waterfall or underwater cave: the skull is absent from that later section of this game. No guns, throwing stars, pumpkins, zombies in party dresses, gore, duplicated skulls or extra fingers. Stunning cinematic realism and strong thumbnail readability.
editPrompt:
Edit the supplied FETCH cover with one precise local correction: the hand on the RIGHT side of the picture is incorrectly mirrored and looks like another left hand. Replace ONLY that right-side hand with an anatomically correct RIGHT HAND belonging to the first-person viewer. Preserve every other part of the picture and its beautiful quality, including the left hand beneath the skull, skull, key, motion light, graveyard, Resident, house, camera, crop, composition, rain, sleeves and moonlight.
The corrected RIGHT forearm enters from the bottom-right corner, exactly where it does now. We see the BACK / DORSAL surface of the right hand as it braces on the vertical wooden doorframe. FOUR fingers extend upward and bend naturally over or against the timber: index nearest the image centre/left, middle next, ring next, pinky on the outside/right. The THUMB MUST emerge from the INNER LEFT EDGE of this hand, pointing left toward the centre of the image and skull, wrapping around the doorway's inner edge. It must NOT sprout from the right edge as it currently does. Clearly show the correct right-hand thumb web, knuckles and natural finger joints, five digits total. Skin wet, dirty, weathered, same adult proportions, with the existing frayed grey coat cuff. Do not rotate a left hand into this space and do not mirror the whole artwork. Replace the right hand with a genuinely correct right hand. Keep the other hand and all background pixels as close as possible to the reference. Preserve the 16:9 landscape composition. No text.
